knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CD-R3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly distinguishes fully Bayesian inference from empirical Bayes inference?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Empirical Bayes estimates prior-level quantities from data, while a full Bayesian model represents their uncertainty probabilistically.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Empirical Bayes plugs in estimated hyperparameters; full Bayes models their uncertainty.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Claiming empirical Bayes has no prior or fully propagates plug-in uncertainty.

choices.label: A fully Bayesian analysis gives prior distributions to hyperparameters, while empirical Bayes estimates some prior hyperparameters from observed data.
Empirical Bayes never uses a prior distribution.
Fully Bayesian inference estimates every prior parameter by maximum likelihood from the same data.
The approaches always produce identical posterior uncertainty.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: conjugate update and Bayes vs EB
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. If X given theta is Binomial(n, theta) and theta has a Beta(alpha, beta) prior, what is the posterior after observing X = x?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Beta-binomial conjugacy adds successes to alpha and failures to beta.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: The posterior is Beta(alpha + x, beta + n - x).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Adding successes to both parameters and ignoring failures.

worked_example.title: Retrieve Beta-Binomial conjugate update
worked_example.problem_statement: Closed-book retrieval of one Bayes hinge. If X | θ ~ Binomial(n = 8, θ) and θ has prior Beta(α, β) = Beta(4, 6), state the posterior after observing X = 2, and refuse one wrong update rule.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Apply Beta-Binomial conjugacy: add successes to α and failures to β.

steps.label: State the conjugate update
steps.explanation: Beta-Binomial conjugacy adds observed successes to α and observed failures to β.

steps.label: Refuse a wrong update
steps.attempt_cue: Name one incorrect parameter update students use.
steps.explanation: Adding n to α and x to β (or adding successes to both parameters) breaks conjugacy. Failures are n - x, not x.
steps.calculation: Refuse Beta(4+8, 6+2) and similar swapped updates

steps.label: Separate full Bayes from EB (light contrast)
steps.attempt_cue: In one sentence, how does empirical Bayes differ?
steps.explanation: Empirical Bayes estimates some prior hyperparameters from data, whereas a fully Bayesian analysis places priors on those hyperparameters and propagates their uncertainty.
steps.calculation: EB plugs in estimated hyperparameters; full Bayes models their uncertainty

worked_example.final_answer: Posterior is Beta(6, 12). Refuse swapped success/failure updates. Empirical Bayes plugs in estimated hyperparameters; full Bayes models their uncertainty.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Updating Beta(α, β) by adding the sample size to α and the success count to β, or claiming empirical Bayes uses no prior.
